introduction: Connecticut legal aid helps eligible residents with civil legal problems. Statewide Legal Services is a starting point for screening and referrals.
description: Connecticut legal aid helps eligible residents with civil legal problems. Statewide Legal Services is a starting point for screening and referrals.

sections.who: Free legal assistance is aimed at people with very low income. The issue, service area and available resources affect whether a program can take a case.
sections.get: Help may include advice or referral to a legal aid office. Separate housing-lawyer intake is available for some eviction and subsidy cases.
sections.docs:
• Court papers and the next deadline or hearing date.
  • Household and income information for screening.
  • Relevant leases, benefit decisions, correspondence and payment records.
sections.apply:
1. Contact Statewide Legal Services

    Call 800-453-3320. The Connecticut Legal Services Get Help page also links to online intake.

  2. Flag housing deadlines

    For eviction or threatened loss of a housing subsidy, call 800-559-1565 or review evictionhelpct.org. Eligibility includes service-area conditions.

  3. Complete the screening

    Explain the issue and provide records the intake worker requests. Clarify whether a lawyer has agreed to represent you.
sections.after: Do not assume an application postpones a hearing. Keep deadlines and ask intake staff what to do while awaiting a decision.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Legal aid contacts; Connecticut Legal Services intake. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Call Statewide Legal Services at 800-453-3320 or use the intake link on the Get Help page.
Some eviction and subsidy matters use 800-559-1565 and the housing-lawyer program.
Can the website webmaster give legal advice?
No. The contact page directs legal requests to Statewide Legal Services.
Where can I read about my rights?
CTLawHelp provides a free self-help library.
